summary: RayFaultTolerance counts never-contacted peers as alive: add_peer seeds every peer with online=True and last_seen=now, so a freshly started coordinator that has never exchanged a single heartbeat considers the full membership alive, self-elects, and authorises writes for a full election_timeout window (10 s default). Sibling of the earlier fail-open heartbeat fix; SplitBrainDetector in core/split_brain.py already fails closed for configured-but-silent peers (is_alive=False at construction) but the election does not.
failure_scenario: 3-node cluster {a,b,c}, b is leader and c follows. Node a restarts while partitioned from b/c (crash, deploy, or its own network not yet up). Within one election round (~2 s) a sees b and c as online, computes alive=3 of 3, self-elects, and can_accept_writes()=True while b is still LEADER and serving writes. Two leaders in one cluster, both accepting writes, for up to 10 s per restart — enough to diverge replicated state. Even with every peer permanently unreachable, the solo survivor self-elects: quorum counts 1 real + N phantom members.
